findings: The delivered audit explicitly rejects the correctness/completeness of the original S6.2 as substantive logic errors. The original row explains precisely that nilpotence of the limit kernel is not necessary for uniqueness and cites S2, while S1/S2 already establish sufficiency under their stated hypotheses. A clearer table heading is an admissible editorial suggestion; it does not establish the alleged substantive reversal. The extra allegations also remove the inherited S1/S2/S4 hypotheses from rows explicitly attributed to those stages. In particular the Z-to-Z/6 example has non-nil kernel6Z and cannot refute S2 under the original common assumptions. The final audit verdict is a source-context error, not an honest coverage omission. These allegations share one decontextualization root.
